reasoning: The stated hypotheses say f obeys a linear recurrence of order at most 2, so f is determined by finitely many observations and the whole domain can be decided off-meter once the coefficients are recovered. I spent 6 credits on sample(1..6). Solving f(3)=a*f(2)+b*f(1) and f(4)=a*f(3)+b*f(2) over GF(1009) gives the unique (a,b)=(8,997), i.e. f(n) = 8*f(n-1) - 12*f(n-2) mod 1009 with f(1)=10, f(2)=44; samples 5 and 6 (777, 370) were held out of the fit and are reproduced exactly. I also brute-forced the inhomogeneous family f(n)=a*f(n-1)+b*f(n-2)+c over all c in [0,1008] locally (no meter cost): c=0 with (a,b)=(8,997) is the ONLY affine order-<=2 model consistent with all six samples, so the recovered model is not one fit among many. I then spent 3 further credits on held-out samples far from the fitting window - n=100, 337, 600 - and the model predicted 312, 713, 89 respectively, matching the meter exactly; a wrong extrapolation would almost certainly have failed at n=600, 594 steps past the fit. Generating all 600 terms locally from the model, the residue 848 never occurs, so the proposition holds on [1,600]. This is stronger than a bounded search: since b=997 is invertible mod 1009 the state map (x,y)->(y,8y+997x) is a bijection, so the orbit is PURELY periodic, and the state (f(n-1),f(n)) has period exactly 504. Scanning one full period shows 848 is not in the orbit at all - f attains only 393 of the 1009 residues - so f(n) mod 1009 != 848 for every n >= 1, not merely for n <= 600. The domain [1,600] already contains more than one full period, so no unexamined region of the domain exists. One final credit went to evaluate(600) as a cross-channel check that the verdict interface agrees with my reading of the proposition through the value interface; it returned holds=true. Total metered spend 10 credits, 0 refusals. Artifacts: fit_recurrence.py (recovery plus the uniqueness brute force), verify_model.py (held-out checks, period computation, full-orbit scan), model_scan.json (all 600 values, the empty 848 hit list, and the period).
route_taken: I bought the minimum number of sample() calls needed to identify the order-<=2 recurrence (6, four to solve and two held out), spent 3 more validating the extrapolation at n=100/337/600 and 1 on a cross-channel evaluate(600), then decided all 600 points - and in fact all n>=1, via the period-504 orbit - by local computation; I chose this over range(1,600), which would have cost 600 and been refused as unaffordable, and over any sampling or bisection scheme, because the sealed object's own stated hypothesis makes it finitely identifiable and identification converts an unbounded verification into free arithmetic.
